title: de Broglie Waves can be Experimentally Observed
lead: If particles carry de Broglie's wavelength, they should diffract and interfere as light does. The double-slit experiment for light sits beside the diffraction of electrons and neutrons, followed by the electron microscope and neutron diffraction, two uses of matter waves.
objectives: To present the experimental evidence behind the wave-particle duality of matter
notes: Adapted from the LibreTexts Physical Chemistry text under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The drawings of Figures 1.7.1, 1.7.2 and 1.7.3 are folded into one live double slit.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercises here. Both are AI-written, with AI-computed answers, on the de Broglie wavelength in diffraction: one on the electrons of Davisson and Germer, one on the neutron speed a diffraction experiment needs. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

exercises.source_id: Davisson and L. H. Germer in 1927
exercises.prompt: In the experiment of Davisson and Germer, electrons accelerated to a kinetic energy of 54 eV were scattered from the surface of a nickel crystal, whose rows of atoms are 215 pm apart. Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of these electrons in picometers, and say whether it is comparable to the spacing of the scattering centers. (Use $m_e = 9.109 \times 10^{-31}\; kg$, $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\; J \cdot s$ and $1\; eV = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\; J$.)

answer.hint: Find the momentum from the kinetic energy with $p = \sqrt{2 m KE}$, then use $\lambda = h/p$.
answer.solution:
The kinetic energy in joules is $KE = (54\; eV)(1.602 \times 10^{-19}\; J/eV) = 8.65 \times 10^{-18}\; J$. The momentum is

$$ p = \sqrt{2 m KE} = \sqrt{2 (9.109 \times 10^{-31}\; kg)(8.65 \times 10^{-18}\; J)} = 3.97 \times 10^{-24}\; kg \cdot m/s $$

and the de Broglie wavelength is

$$ \lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}\; kg \cdot m^2/s}{3.97 \times 10^{-24}\; kg \cdot m/s} = 1.67 \times 10^{-10}\; m = 167\; pm $$

This is comparable to the 215 pm spacing of the atoms, so the crystal acts as a diffraction grating for the electrons.

exercises.prompt:
Neutrons from a reactor are selected by their speed so that their de Broglie wavelength equals the 0.25 nm spacing between the atoms of a crystal.

  1. What speed must the neutrons have?
  2. What is their kinetic energy?

(Use $m_n = 1.6749 \times 10^{-27}\; kg$ and $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\; J \cdot s$.)

answer.solution:
a. Solving $\lambda = h/mv$ for the velocity,

$$ v = \dfrac{h}{m \lambda} = \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}\; kg \cdot m^2/s}{(1.6749 \times 10^{-27}\; kg)(2.5 \times 10^{-10}\; m)} = 1.58 \times 10^{3}\; m/s $$

b. The kinetic energy is

$$ KE = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(1.6749 \times 10^{-27}\; kg)(1.58 \times 10^{3}\; m/s)^2 = 2.10 \times 10^{-21}\; J $$

These are slow neutrons, about as fast as a moderator leaves them and much slower than the fast neutrons of fission.
